raw.title: Strategic Industry Expert
raw.excerpt: The Strategic Industry Expert (SIE) is a senior role for a recognised market expert who works with Fastmarkets’ largest forest products customers.
raw.description:
The Strategic Industry Expert (SIE) is a senior role for a recognised market expert who works with Fastmarkets’ largest forest products customers. The SIE will have an overall responsibility to driving a market informed growth strategy and elevating our positioning with some of our largest customers. The role also links them with our commercial, editorial and analytics teams.

This role is part of Fastmarkets’ Strategic Industry Expertise (SIE) team, a central team that works across our whole customer base. SIEs work with the most senior stakeholders/C-suite at our largest customers as market experts and thought partners, and help those customers get more out of Fastmarkets in the decisions that matter most to their business.

The Americas role covers pulp, paper, packaging, tissue, recovered paper and wood products across North and Latin America. The focus is the Americas, but you will also support global customers, working with SIE and commercial colleagues in EMEA and APAC. The role needs someone with deep knowledge of these markets, a strong network in the region, and the credibility to hold a market conversation with a CEO or other senior stakeholders in customer organisations.

The Americas are central to global forest products. North America is the largest containerboard and softwood lumber market in the world, while Brazil and Chile have the world’s lowest-cost hardwood pulp capacity, which sets the pace for global market pulp supply. Fastmarkets prices are the benchmarks behind billions of dollars of pulp, paper, packaging and wood products contracts in the region. These markets are changing quickly. The SIE needs to understand these changes in detail, because they shape what customers need from Fastmarkets.

You will work with customers across the value chain, including pulp, paper, packaging and wood producers; converters; packaging buyers at large consumer goods, food and retail companies; home improvement retailers and lumber dealers; traders; and banks and investors. You will build a clear picture of each customer group’s strategic objectives and challenges and how the Fastmarkets’ offering portfolio can help address those objectives and challenges – these span across purchasing, sales, planning and risk decisions. You will engage with customers in many different ways, from C-suite meetings and strategy workshops to presentations, regional roadshows and speaking at industry conferences.

The ideal candidate will be a recognised market expert (from a PRA, or other well known market intelligence providers in forest products, or leading industry players in forest products), who also has a good understanding of Fastmarkets offerings and has a good network in the market.

This is a senior role and requires the candidate to drive our positioning in the external market. You will be joining a highly influential SIE team that sits at the heart of our growth strategy.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Support the growth of Fastmarkets in key forest products customer segments (pulp, paper, packaging and wood products) across North and Latin America. These include, but are not limited to, forest producers, downstream customers for whom packaging or wood products are critical, traders, and banks and financial institutions. You will also support global customers with operations in the Americas and other regions.
  • Own and present in-depth strategic insights to senior stakeholders and decision makers in customer organizations, positioned as authoritative Fastmarkets points of view (PoVs), and show how Fastmarkets’ solutions meet specific customer objectives. This includes C-suite meetings, presentations, roadshows and industry events.
  • Drive significant revenue growth by identifying opportunities to expand our business through:
    • supporting successful commercial wins with key existing customers in the Americas, by adding value through targeted engagement and by embedding our products and services more deeply in their workflows
    • expanding our value proposition with customers to create new opportunities across our wider suite of analytical offerings in pulp, paper, packaging and wood products
  • Collaborate with Account Managers and Commercial teams to drive revenue growth, act as value owner for high-value renewals, and help run the Forest pricing desk.
  • Establish a strong network of senior stakeholders across our Americas customer base, networking actively across the industry to develop valuable connections.
  • Develop and own a strategic view of the market conditions (headwinds and tailwinds) that affect our customer base and how we position ourselves to drive revenue growth, including competitive intelligence for Forest in the Americas.
  • Work closely with cross-functional teams to refine strategies, improve product offerings and provide enhanced customer support in the region.
  • Keep the Forest sales team up to date on market developments through a regular market meeting, and help onboard new colleagues.
  • Conduct and document high-impact pre- and post-sales activities, ensuring comprehensive client engagement, and contribute to the internal quarterly and annual sales and financial planning cycles.
  • Travel as required for client meetings, conferences and regional roadshows.

We recruit talented, dynamic people with diverse backgrounds and experiences, all united by a belief in our mission to provide the world’s leading and most trusted price reporting, events, and intelligence service for the markets we serve. We’re proud to be an equal opportunities employer and are committed to creating a fully inclusive workplace, where everyone feels able to participate and contribute meaningfully.

If you are open-minded, curious, resilient, solutions-oriented and committed to promoting equality, then read on.

KNOWLEDGE, EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS

We are looking for an individual who is highly motivated, driven, and have a passion to be part of a fast-paced, successful team. Being a strong team player is also important as well as someone who is happy to work flexibly.

  • A wealth of experience in North American and/or Latin American forest products markets (pulp, paper, packaging, tissue, recovered paper or wood products), with a strong track record.
  • That experience could come from a price reporting agency, as a market expert or price reporter, or from work as an economist or market analyst.
  • Alternatively, you may have worked at a major forest products producer in a commercial, market analysis or strategy role, in packaging procurement at a large consumer goods, food or retail company, or in forest products equity research, banking or investing.
  • A working understanding of how price data is used in this industry: index-linked contracts, cost models, budgeting and forecasting, risk management and valuation.
  • Credibility with senior stakeholders and the confidence to present to small groups and large audiences alike.
  • Sound commercial judgment. A sales background is not required, but you should be comfortable taking part in renewal and pricing conversations and working closely with account managers.
  • Strong analytical skills, including the ability to build your own analysis and presentations and to use AI tools to work faster.
  • A team player who works well across commercial, editorial, analytics and product teams.
  • An established network of contacts in the Americas forest products industry is desirable.
  • Fluency in English. Spanish or Portuguese is a plus.

If you're excited about the role but your experience, skills or qualifications don't perfectly align, we encourage you to apply anyway.

Our Values

Fastmarkets people come from all different walks of life. It’s this mix of brilliant personalities, experiences and insights that gives us that warm, open, and friendly culture you can feel as soon as you meet us. But however wonderfully different we all are, there are six things we all have in common – and they form our Fastmarkets values.

Created by our own employees to reflect some of the personal traits that Fastmarkets people have, our values are key to what makes our culture unique. They reflect who each of us are and they're embedded in everything we do. Our values are:

  • METRICS DRIVEN. We use insights to improve our customers’ experience and our business performance
  • ACCOUNTABLE. We are accountable to ourselves and those we work with: we keep our promises and get things done
  • GROWTH MINDSET. This value enables us to be nimble to the changing realities and operate with a sense of urgency
  • INCLUSIVE. We are inclusive and respectful, celebrating each of us and giving everyone a deep sense of belonging with the desire to bring their best self to work every day.
  • CUSTOMER CENTRIC. We are customer-centric in all that we do
  • COLLABORATIVE. We are collaborative, able to work across teams and capitalise on the diversity of intellect, perspectives, and experiences.

We are committed to ensuring all candidates feel welcomed and supported. Should your application advance and you require accommodations for the interview process, please inform us so we can make the necessary arrangements.

Reward and benefits at Fastmarkets

We believe in fair pay and benefits that support you both inside and outside of work. Through Fastmarkets Rewards, you'll have access to a range of core benefits and a flexible allowance, giving you the freedom to tailor your package to suit your lifestyle, wellbeing and financial priorities. We know that everyone's needs are different, so we've designed our benefits to support our diverse global team wherever they're based.

Specific benefits may vary by country and role.

If the position is listed as remote this opportunity is available to applicants based in the following states:

• Illinois

• Oregon

• New York
• Pennsylvania

• Texas*

* Denotes states with office locations to support hybrid working.

Otherwise the position will be located as shown in the advert.

You’ve read a little about us – now it’s over to you!

If you like what you’ve read so far and think you can see yourself as a Fastmarkets person, it’s time to fill in your application form. This form is an important part of the selection process: it’s used to determine whether or not you’ll be chosen to have an interview and acts as a basis for the questions we’ll ask you on the day.

It’s vital that you try to capture all the relevant information we have asked for on the form so we can get a good feel for who you are and why you’re great.

Fastmarkets is an industry-leading price-reporting agency (PRA) and information provider for global commodities, providing price data, news, analytics and events for the agriculture, forest products, metals and mining and new-generation energy markets.

Fastmarkets' data is critical for customers seeking to understand and predict dynamic, sometimes opaque markets, enabling trading and risk management. Fastmarkets is a global business with a history dating back to 1865 and is built on trust and deep market knowledge. It has more than 700 employees spread across global locations in the UK, US, China, India, Singapore, Brazil, Belgium, Bulgaria, Finland and beyond.

raw.description:
Job Description

A bit about this role:

Accurate, complete, and timely provider data is foundational to how we serve our members and support our providers. It powers the provider directory, helps members find and navigate care, reduces administrative burden for providers, and supports critical processes including claims, utilization management, credentialing, network operations, care navigation, and reporting. Because provider data is complex, interconnected, and constantly changing, strong processes to monitor, verify, and improve its accuracy are essential to our member and provider experiences, operational performance, and compliance with federal and state requirements.


The Manager will help drive operational excellence across the provider data lifecycle—from onboarding and initial configuration through ongoing maintenance and verification—with particular focus on ensuring that records affecting member care are accurate, complete, and up to date. By connecting operational insights, stakeholder feedback, and data trends, this person will identify opportunities to strengthen processes, improve data quality, and prevent issues before they impact members, providers, or downstream business operations. We’re looking for a self-starter who can bring structure to ambiguous problems, manage multiple initiatives, and move work from insight to implementation.


Your responsibilities and impact will include:

  • Support and advance initiatives that improve the accuracy, completeness, timeliness, and scalability of provider and facility data operations from onboarding through ongoing maintenance and verification
  • Help oversee the operating performance of offshore teams and automated solutions supporting provider data and verification initiatives, including monitoring quality, productivity, capacity, and issue trends
  • Develop and maintain reporting, dashboards, and monitoring that provide visibility into operational performance, verification results, data quality trends, emerging risks, and opportunities for intervention
  • Partner with product and engineering to define requirements, test enhancements, and improve the usability, accuracy, and scalability of verification tools and workflows
  • Help design, build, and monitor AI agents and other automation solutions that improve the efficiency, scalability, and accuracy of provider data operations and initiatives
  • Analyze root causes of recurring data issues and recommend process, tooling, or upstream improvements that prevent issues from recurring
  • Partner with claims and other internal data teams to develop reporting and analyses that quantify the operational and business impact of provider data issues
  • Serve as a flexible operational leader who can build structure in ambiguous environments, take on new problem areas, and shift priorities as business and member needs evolve

Required skills and experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree and 3–5+ years of relevant experience in healthcare operations, provider data, provider directory, credentialing, claims, network operations, data quality, or a related field
  • Experience managing operational workflows involving provider data, record validation, data quality, research, verification, or issue remediation
  • Demonstrated ability to build, document, and scale repeatable operational processes with measurable quality and productivity outcomes
  • Strong analytical skills, including the ability to investigate data issues, identify patterns and anomalies, and translate findings into clear operational actions
  • Experience building or maintaining dashboards, reporting, or monitoring tools to identify risks and track performance
  • Experience partnering with product and engineering teams to define requirements, test enhancements, and improve operational tooling
  • Strong project management, communication, and organizational skills, with the ability to prioritize competing needs and work effectively with offshore teams and cross-functional partners
  • Self-directed and comfortable operating in a fast-paced, metrics-driven environment with ambiguity and evolving priorities

Desired skills and experience:

  • Experience managing or scaling offshore, vendor, or shared-services teams
  • Experience applying AI, agentic workflows, machine learning, or automation to reduce manual operational work
  • SQL or equivalent ability to query, join, and validate provider, claims, or operational data directly
  • Familiarity with provider directory requirements, CMS Medicare Advantage directory accuracy expectations, or other healthcare data and network regulations

Salary Range: $73,000-$115,000/year

The pay range listed for this position is the range the organization reasonably and in good faith expects to pay for this position at the time of the posting. Once the interview process begins, your talent partner will provide additional information on the compensation for the role, along with additional information on our total rewards package. The actual base salary offered will depend on a variety of factors, including the qualifications of the individual applicant for the position, years of relevant experience, specific and unique skills, level of education attained, certifications or other professional licenses held, and the location in which the applicant lives and/or from which they will be performing the job.

Our Total Rewards package includes:

  • Employer sponsored health, dental and vision plan with low or no premium

  • Generous paid time off

  • $100 monthly mobile or internet stipend

  • Stock options for all employees

  • Bonus eligibility for all roles excluding Director and above; Commission eligibility for Sales roles

  • Parental leave program

  • 401K program

  • And more....

*Our total rewards package is for full time employees only. Intern and Contract positions are not eligible.

Founded in 2017, Devoted Health is on a mission to dramatically improve the health and well-being of older Americans by caring for everyone like they are family, and that includes our employees. Our robust and seamlessly integrated care platform merges advanced data and AI access with world-class clinical and service experiences to create a member experience that is unlike the industry norm. To continue building upon our mission, we want to bring together those who share our values, embrace change and advancement, and are enthusiastic about where we're going — all the while bringing their own unique qualities, experiences, and expertise, in hopes of further changing the healthcare experience.


Devoted is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to a safe and supportive work environment in which all employees have the opportunity to participate and contribute to the success of the business. We value diversity and collaboration. Individuals are respected for their skills, experience, and unique perspectives. This commitment is embodied in Devoted’s Code of Conduct, our company values and the way we do business.


As an Equal Opportunity Employer, the Company does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy status, marital status, national origin, disability, age, sexual orientation, veteran status, genetic information, gender identity, gender expression, or any other factor prohibited by law. Our management team is dedicated to this policy with respect to recruitment, hiring, placement, promotion, transfer, training, compensation, benefits, employee activities and general treatment during employment.

★ PLEASE SUBMIT YOUR CV IN ENGLISH ★

Litigation Paralegal

Location: Costa Rica
Work Arrangement: Fully Remote, Full-Time (9:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. U.S. Eastern Time)
Employment Type: Independent Contractor
Industry: Legal Services / Law Firm
Compensation: $10–$12 USD per hour
Experience: 5+ Years
English Proficiency: Advanced English (Subject to Confirmation)

About the Company

Our client is an established U.S.-based law firm with decades of experience in personal injury and criminal defense representation.

The firm represents injury victims in cases such as car and truck accidents, slip and falls, premises liability, wrongful death, and dog bites, and also provides criminal defense. It works with a seasoned team of trial attorneys and legal support staff, and it is committed to professionalism, responsiveness, and strong results for its clients.

The firm is looking to grow its remote support team with legally trained professionals from Latin America.

About the Role

We are looking for a proactive, detail-oriented, and legally trained Litigation Paralegal to support the firm's personal injury litigation practice, ideally an attorney or law graduate who wants to apply their legal education and experience in a remote paralegal role.

You will support the Personal Injury Litigation Attorney with case management, discovery, filings, medical records, liens, settlement preparation, client communication, and administrative tasks, while escalating legal decisions to U.S.-licensed counsel.

This role is ideal for someone who is organized, fluent in professional English, and able to manage routine case needs independently while working under attorney supervision.

Why This Opportunity?

  • Work directly with a U.S. trial law firm on active personal injury litigation.
  • Gain practical exposure to U.S. litigation, discovery, medical records, liens, and settlement processes.
  • Develop your case management, documentation, and client communication skills.
  • Work fully remotely with U.S. Eastern Time business hours.
  • Join a growing team with opportunities to learn and take on greater responsibility.

What You'll Do

Litigation & Case Management

  • Assist with pleadings, discovery, correspondence, court filings, and service of process.
  • Track open records requests, affidavits of service, court deadlines, and case calendars.
  • Monitor cases, identify outstanding tasks, and escalate issues requiring attorney attention.

Medical Records & Documentation

  • Request, organize, and track medical records and billing statements.
  • Follow up with providers and prepare medical treatment and billing summaries.
  • Identify missing documentation and maintain complete case files.

Liens & Settlement Support

  • Conduct lien lookups and coordinate Medicaid requests.
  • Track medical liens, balances, and settlement obligations.
  • Prepare settlement distribution statements and closing documents for attorney review.

Client Communication & Administration

  • Communicate with clients, providers, insurers, opposing offices, process servers, and government agencies.
  • Draft routine correspondence and follow up on outstanding documents and requests.
  • Maintain electronic files, case notes, calendars, and expense records.
  • Assist with filings, service fees, incoming correspondence, and other case-related administrative tasks.

Qualifications

Required

  • 5+ years of relevant legal experience.
  • Law degree from a recognized university in Mexico or another Latin American country; licensed attorneys are encouraged to apply.
  • Advanced written and spoken English proficiency.
  • Strong legal research, drafting, organization, document review, and deadline-management skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple cases independently and provide accurate status updates.
  • Reliable internet, a private workspace, and commitment to confidentiality and information security.

Preferred

  • Experience with a U.S. law firm, personal injury litigation, or civil litigation.
  • Knowledge of discovery, pleadings, court filings, service of process, and litigation calendars; Georgia procedure experience is a plus.
  • Experience with medical records, billing, liens, and settlement documentation.
  • Familiarity with MyCase or similar case-management software.

How Success Is Measured

  • Accurate case files and timely completion of assignments.
  • Reliable calendaring and deadline tracking.
  • Consistent follow-up and professional communication.
  • Accurate documentation and proactive litigation support.
  • Organization, reliability, and proactive communication with the team.

Why Join Us

You'll join a collaborative, fully remote support team that values ownership, professionalism, clear communication, and continuous professional development.

The firm offers hands-on exposure to U.S. personal injury litigation, close work with experienced trial attorneys, and opportunities to grow your expertise in litigation support.

Important Notes

  • This is a paralegal and legal support position, not a U.S. attorney position.
  • All work is performed under attorney supervision. The position does not authorize independent U.S. legal advice, attorney representation, legal strategy decisions, or unsupervised legal practice. Substantive legal questions and settlement advice must be referred to the assigned attorney.
  • The position requires strong ownership of tasks, attention to detail, and reliable follow-through.
  • Shortlisted candidates may be asked to complete a written English and legal-support skills assessment.
  • Please submit your CV in English, detailing your legal education, bar admission or professional credentials (if applicable), English proficiency, and relevant litigation or U.S. law firm experience.

This is a fully remote position.

raw.description:
Job Description Summary

The Senior Staff Technical Program Manager – Infrastructure and Platform will be a key leader in a new AI enablement team within our defense systems business. The team’s mission is to accelerate time-to-value with AI by enabling safe, scalable experimentation and maturing successful pilots into enterprise-grade solutions.

In this role, you will partner closely with business stakeholders and multiple DT/technical teams to define scope, requirements, and execution plans that enable deployment and integration of AI and related technologies. You will own program execution end-to-end, driving clarity, alignment, and transparency across all parties. The successful candidate will embody an innovators DNA Handler mindset: proactive, resourceful, bias to action, and relentlessly focused on turning AI potential into measurable outcomes.

Job Description

Key Responsibilities:

Program and backlog management

  • Own the platform product backlog and intake: how platform work is requested, prioritized, sequenced, and released
  • Translate the Director's roadmap into a resourced plan with physical dates and one named owner per action
  • Run the daily management, WOR, and MOR cadence for the platform team — managing the plan to Green rather than reporting status

Golden-path adoption

  • Drive adoption of the single golden-path delivery pipeline across the four product-development teams, tracking adoption and removing friction
  • Coordinate the onboarding of teams onto shared services and the paved road, with clear entry criteria and support

Stakeholder and dependency management

  • Manage dependencies between the platform team and the product and architecture teams without formal authority, using transparent intake and prioritization criteria
  • Broker trade-offs and surface conflicts early, escalating with options attached rather than letting dates slip silently

Standard work and metrics

  • Define and maintain the standard work for platform intake, change, and release
  • Instrument platform adoption, reliability, and delivery metrics (including DORA) and report them into the operating rhythm

Basic qualifications (required)

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited university or college with a minimum of 5 years of professional experience OR Associate's degree with a minimum of 8 years of professional experience OR High School Diploma with a minimum of 10 years of professional experience.
  • Minimum 5 years of professional experience in Technical Program Management or IT.
  • Note: Military experience is equivalent to professional experience.

Eligibility requirement

  • Legal authorization to work in the U.S. is required. GE Aerospace will not sponsor individuals for employment visas, now or in the future, for this job.

Desired characteristics (preferred, not mandatory)

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field.
  • Certified Scrum Product Owner (CSPO), SAFe Agilist or Product Owner, or PMP certification.
  • Experience managing an infrastructure, platform, or DevOps program as a product, including backlog and roadmap ownership.
  • Working knowledge of CI/CD, cloud environments, and the mechanics of a golden-path delivery pipeline.
  • Demonstrated ability to drive adoption of a shared standard across teams that do not report to you.
  • Fluency instrumenting and reporting delivery metrics, including DORA (lead time, deployment frequency, change failure rate, time-to-restore).
  • FLIGHT DECK, Lean, or a comparable operating-cadence discipline.
  • Defense, aerospace, or other regulated-industry background.

Success metrics

  • Golden-path adoption across the four product-development teams
  • Platform backlog delivered within planned capacity, with dates held rather than silently moved
  • Intake-to-start time for a new platform request
  • Delivery-metric trend (DORA) for teams on the platform
  • Operating-cadence health: plan managed proactively, escalations raised early

Why this role

  • A platform only pays off if teams actually use it and the work behind it stays on plan. This role owns both: the front door for platform demand and the cadence that keeps delivery predictable. You will turn a roadmap into a managed program, drive a shared standard across teams you do not control, and hold the plan to standard work.

Notes:

The base pay range for this position is $131, 000 to $189,000 annually. The specific pay offered may be influenced by a variety of factors, including the candidate’s experience, education, and skill set. This position is also eligible for an annual discretionary bonus based on a percentage of your base salary/ commission based on the plan. This posting is expected to close on November 2nd, 2026.

GE Aerospace offers comprehensive benefits and programs to support your health and, along with programs like HealthAhead, your physical, emotional, financial and social wellbeing. Healthcare benefits include medical, dental, vision, and prescription drug coverage; access to a Health Coach from GE Aerospace; and the Employee Assistance Program, which provides 24/7 confidential assessment, counseling and referral services. Retirement benefits include the GE Aerospace Retirement Savings Plan, a 401(k) savings plan with company matching contributions and company retirement contributions, as well as access to Fidelity resources and planning consultants. Other benefits include tuition assistance, adoption assistance, paid parental leave, disability insurance, life insurance, and paid time-off for vacation or illness.

GE Aerospace (General Electric Company or the Company) and its affiliates each sponsor certain employee benefit plans or programs (i.e., is a “Sponsor”). Each Sponsor reserves the right to terminate, amend, suspend, replace or modify its benefit plans and programs at any time and for any reason, in its sole discretion. No individual has a vested right to any benefit under a Sponsor’s welfare benefit plan or program. This document does not create a contract of employment with any individual.

This role requires access to U.S. export-controlled information. Therefore, employment will be contingent upon the ability to prove that you meet the status of a U.S. Person as one of the following: U.S. lawful permanent resident, U.S. Citizen, have been granted asylee or refugee status (i.e., a protected individual under the Immigration and Naturalization Act, 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3)).

Additional Information

GE Aerospace offers a great work environment, professional development, challenging careers, and competitive compensation. GE Aerospace is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law.

Any offer of employment is conditioned upon the successful completion of a drug screen (as applicable). Employees may also be subject to random and reasonable-suspicion drug and alcohol testing.

The Associate Director, Process Improvement is responsible for evaluating the effectiveness of existing business processes and leading the development of sustainable, repeatable, and measurable improvements. This role oversees a team of process improvement professionals and CRM User Acceptance Testing (UAT) testers, with accountability for ensuring CRM-related processes are well documented, thoroughly tested, and continuously optimized to improve both operational efficiency and the consumer experience.
This leader provides strategic support the VA contract with a focus on product and process implementation, service operations, contract compliance, and continuous improvement through design thinking, process mapping, and process modeling. The Associate Director is also expected to partner across both lines of business to identify, share, and implement best practices and lessons learned from one area to the other.

Key responsibilities include:


  • Leading a team of process improvement professionals and CRM UAT testers to advance process optimization, testing effectiveness, and quality outcomes.

  • Ensuring processes are comprehensively documented and routinely assessed across people, process, and technology to identify and implement improvement opportunities.

  • Promoting compliance, consistency, and operational excellence.
  • Applying strong leadership, communication, technical expertise, and innovative solution design to improve performance, mitigate risk, and achieve compliance and financial objectives.

This role requires a strategic, forward-thinking leader who can drive change, foster continuous improvement, and balance operational efficiency with an enhanced consumer experience.

The Product Manager, Clinical Content will drive the development and success of our healthcare ambulatory software products. This role will be responsible for managing one or more products and leading initiatives to enhance our solutions for outpatient care environments. This role will lead cross-functional product and engineering teams to deliver high-impact features and drive strategic initiatives.

  • Define and prioritize product features based on user needs, market trends, client value, anticipated outcomes, and business objectives.
  • Coordinate with engineering, design, and other teams to ensure timely and successful product delivery.
  • Analyze market data and user feedback to drive product improvements and innovations.
  • Play a significant role in managing the product lifecycle from ideation to product sunset, including requirements gathering, prioritization, development, launch, and phase outs.
  • Collaborate with sales, marketing, and customer support teams to ensure alignment and successful product adoption.
  • Prepare and present product performance reports and metrics.

  • Proven track record of successful product launches and management.
  • Experience with agile methodologies and product management tools.
  • Experience with ambulatory care software or EHR systems preferred.

  • Knowledge of: Strong understanding of both healthcare and technology. Strong understanding of product management principles and software development life cycle. Knowledge of healthcare regulations and compliance requirements.

Want to design the architecture that lets AI agents safely refactor, test and ship production code? Then let's talk.

Our client acquires enterprise software companies and turns them into AI-native, profitable, scalable businesses. They are a remote-first, AI-forward team spread across the globe, offering high ownership, flexibility and impact, work across multiple products and technologies, and growth pathways across engineering, product and leadership.

The job: transform a 10+ year legacy codebase into a high-velocity, agent-operable architecture, at the intersection of software architecture, AI-agent orchestration and engineering governance.

Contract Type: Contract, full-time

Location: Fully remote from Eastern Europe, working US morning hours (Scrum).

What you'll do

Agent-operable system architecture

  • Decompose legacy monoliths into agent-readable, modular systems with strict boundaries and single responsibility

  • Lead incremental modernization using the Strangler Pattern, wrapping legacy logic in modern, contract-driven interfaces

  • Enforce SOLID principles, Dependency Injection, and Hexagonal Architecture to ensure deterministic AI execution and low regression risk

Agentic framework & MCP leadership

  • Architect and maintain the agent context layer: standardized Skills, Rules, and Commands for AI-driven engineering workflows

  • Build and operate Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers exposing legacy APIs, services, and databases as typed, secure, AI-consumable tools

  • Own contract-first API design as the primary interface between human intent and autonomous agent execution

Engineering governance & AI quality control

  • Act as architectural gatekeeper for AI-generated pull requests, ensuring scalability, security, and long-term maintainability

  • Mandate test-driven development (TDD) and characterization testing to preserve legacy behavior during refactoring

  • Monitor and optimize agentic reasoning loops to balance cost, speed, and architectural integrity

What we're looking for

  • 4+ years in software architecture, platform engineering, or technical leadership

  • Proven experience modernizing large, undocumented legacy systems

  • Deep hands-on expertise with TypeScript, .NET, and Node.js

  • Strong background in API design, distributed systems, and modular architectures

  • Practical experience with agentic development, MCP, LLM tooling, or AI-assisted engineering

  • Bias toward clean code, deterministic systems, and production-grade AI

Nice to have

  • Experience with remote-first or globally distributed teams

  • Background in SaaS transformations, scale-ups, or PE-backed environments

  • Comfort operating in high-ambiguity, high-ownership settings
